key_insight: AI scientists struggle to reproduce quantum research from papers alone, but externally verified workflow repairs can become reusable experience that improves performance.
engineering_relevance: Verified, reusable workflows could make computational quantum research automation more reliable and cost-effective without changing the underlying model.
method: Build OmniQ, an expert-audited environment that turns published studies into executable reproduction tasks.
Use Residual Agents to distil externally verified workflow repairs into reusable research experience.
Expose reproduced results and verified workflows through an extensible Model Context Protocol platform.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 59 papers, five LLM-powered agentic systems and six third-party harnesses; Residual Agents raised reported DeepSeek V4.1 Flash performance from 68% to 85%, matching Claude Code with Opus 5 at one-third of its cost.
watch_item: The approach depends on external verification and expert-informed repairs; gains on reproduction tasks do not yet establish autonomous discovery capability.
paper_title: Reimagining computational quantum research with AI scientists
